question: What is the primary focus of quality assurance in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment purchases
options.C: Proactive monitoring and continuous improvement of patient care
options.D: Punishing nurses who make clinical documentation errors

explanation: Quality assurance focuses on systematic, proactive steps to monitor and improve care delivery rather than just punishing mistakes after they happen. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h1)

question: How does quality improvement differ from quality control?

options.A: Quality improvement is done by doctors while quality control is done by nurses
options.B: Quality improvement happens annually while quality control happens every decade
options.C: Quality improvement redesigns systems proactively while quality control inspects after the fact
options.D: Quality improvement focuses only on finances while quality control focuses on patients

explanation: Quality control acts as a reactive check for errors, whereas quality improvement continuously redesigns processes to prevent those errors from happening. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h1)

question: A standard that focuses on the physical environment and equipment of a hospital is called what?
explanation: Structure standards look at the framework of care, including facilities, equipment, and staff qualifications. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h2)

question: Evaluating whether a patient develops a pressure ulcer after two weeks of nursing care measures which type of standard?
explanation: Outcome standards measure the final result of care and the actual change in the patient's health status. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which phase of the nursing process involves gathering baseline physiological data from the patient?
explanation: Assessment is the initial step where the nurse systematically collects and records patient data. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: What happens during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

options.A: The nurse checks if patient goals were met and adjusts the care plan
options.B: The nurse writes down the medical diagnosis given by the doctor
options.C: The nurse administers prescribed medications to the ward patients
options.D: The nurse organizes the physical equipment needed for a procedure

explanation: Evaluation measures patient progress against established goals to see if interventions worked or need revision. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is it important to integrate clinical standards into the nursing process?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to document patient vitals
options.B: It allows doctors to bypass writing direct medical prescriptions
options.C: It reduces practice variations and ensures consistent evidence-based care
options.D: It speeds up the hospital discharge financial billing process

explanation: Standardization ensures that care is consistent, safe, and based on proven evidence rather than personal preference. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h4)

question: Standardized care plans are primarily used during which phase of the nursing process?
explanation: Standardized care plans guide the selection of appropriate goals and interventions during the planning phase. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of an incident report in a hospital ward?

options.A: To document adverse events and near-misses for quality review
options.B: To calculate the monthly salary of the nursing staff
options.C: To record the medical history given by a new patient
options.D: To request pharmaceutical drug supplies from the pharmacy

explanation: Incident reports capture errors and near-misses so the facility can analyze root causes and prevent recurrence. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h5)

question: A tool used to review patient case notes to check if required nursing actions were performed is called a what?
explanation: Nursing audits systematically examine documentation and patient records to measure compliance with established standards. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which body is legally responsible for setting nursing educational standards in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory regulatory body mandated to set educational and practice standards for Nigerian nurses. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of the mandatory continuing professional development (MCPD) program?

options.A: To determine the salary scale for nurses working in federal hospitals
options.B: To serve as the primary licensure examination for newly graduated students
options.C: To inspect hospital wards for structural and environmental cleanliness
options.D: To ensure practicing nurses keep their clinical skills and knowledge updated

explanation: MCPD programs ensure that registered nurses maintain competence and stay current with modern healthcare practices throughout their careers. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why is a non-punitive reporting culture important for successful quality assurance?

options.A: It allows the hospital to avoid paying financial penalties for mistakes
options.B: It eliminates the need for nurses to write incident reports altogether
options.C: It encourages staff to report errors openly so systems can be fixed
options.D: It ensures that patients never experience any complications during care

explanation: When staff fear punishment, they hide mistakes, making it impossible to analyze root causes and improve the system. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge to quality assurance in Nigerian healthcare?

options.A: Heavy workload leading to staff burnout
options.B: Excessive availability of advanced medical equipment
options.C: Severe shortages of qualified nursing personnel

explanation: Resource scarcity and equipment shortages are major challenges, whereas excess equipment is not a typical problem in public facilities. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h7)
